findings.issue_text: Accidental git submodule `sentry-repo` (gitlink, mode 160000) added at repo root with no corresponding `.gitmodules` entry, causing fresh clones and CI checkouts to fail with 'No submodule mapping found in .gitmodules'

`options.get("issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist", [])` passes `[]` as the `silent` parameter rather than a default value, so an unregistered option raises `UnknownOption` (uncaught by `handle_query_errors`), causing the /events-stats endpoint to 500 for all users

Substring check `"event.type:error" in query` matches negated or OR-composed filters (e.g. `!event.type:error`), applying the sample-weight transform to transaction events where `sample_weight` is not meaningful, yielding wrong counts or query failures

`upsampled_count` SnQLFunction is only registered on the DiscoverDataset function converter, but the transform is enabled for the `errors` dataset, so queries flowing through the errors dataset fail with an unknown-function error

Upsampling eligibility decision inspects `request.GET.get("query")` instead of the query parameter actually executed, so dashboard widgets (dashboardWidgetId flow) silently never get upsampling and mixed inputs use the wrong query string

`invalidate_upsampling_cache` is never called anywhere in the diff and its cache key scheme (org id + hash of exact project-id tuple) cannot invalidate allowlist changes, leaving stale upsampled results for up to 60s after a project is removed from the allowlist

In the top-events branch, only `query_columns` is transformed; `equations` and `orderby` containing `count()` are left untransformed, producing inconsistent weighted vs unweighted numbers in the same response and potentially breaking orderby resolution against the `upsampled_count() as count` column

Naive substring check in _is_error_focused_query ("event.type:error" in query.lower()) misroutes non-error queries (negation like !event.type:error, mixed OR queries, literal text matches) into the upsampling transform, rewriting count() to sum(sample_weight) which doesn't exist for transaction events, causing user-triggerable Snuba 500s or silently wrong statistics; should parse the query via the search backend instead of substring-matching raw input

Accidental git submodule 'sentry-repo' committed at repo root (mode 160000, gitlink) unrelated to the feature with no corresponding .gitmodules entry; should be removed before merge as it breaks submodule initialization/CI and is a repo-integrity/supply-chain hygiene issue

upsampled_count SnQLFunction registered without a private flag (unlike adjacent failure_count), allowing any authenticated user to invoke it directly in discover-dataset queries for any project, bypassing the endpoint-level allowlist gating and potentially producing Snuba errors (unknown column on entities lacking sample_weight) or misleading counts

Cache key built from Python hash() of the sorted project-ID tuple is collision-prone by design; two different project sets hashing to the same value would be served the wrong eligibility decision (upsampling applied to a non-allowlisted set or vice versa); should use a deterministic, collision-resistant encoding such as sorted IDs joined

invalidate_upsampling_cache is dead code (defined but never called) and nothing subscribes to allowlist changes, so after a project is removed from the allowlist the eligibility cache continues authorizing the sum(sample_weight) transform for up to 60 seconds, exactly the window where the sample_weight data guarantee is being withdrawn

Client-supplied contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate drives upsampled counts via sum(sample_weight); if production ingestion mirrors the factory, any SDK/client can report an arbitrarily small sample rate to inflate its project's upsampled error counts without bound, compromising data integrity of stats/alerting (needs verification against the actual ingestion path)

Caching an in-memory options lookup with memcached/redis adds network round-trips (a GET on every request plus a SET on every miss) to the hot /events-stats endpoint, replacing a sub-microsecond local dict lookup with per-request network I/O — a negative optimization

Cache key embeds the exact sorted project-ID set (hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))), so any query with a different project subset is a guaranteed cache miss, yielding poor hit rates and two network ops for most requests; key should be coarse (e.g., org-level allowlist snapshot) or the cache dropped entirely

Substring matching in _is_error_focused_query ('event.type:error' in query.lower()) incorrectly matches negated queries (!event.type:error) and mixed queries (event.type:transaction OR event.type:error), applying the sum(sample_weight) transform to non-error events and producing silently wrong data (negated charts render 0, mixed queries undercount)

O(P × A) linear membership scan in _are_all_projects_error_upsampled: all(project_id in allowlist ...) scans the allowlist list per project, costing potentially tens of ms on hot paths for org-wide queries; fix by converting allowlist to a set
sentry-repo submodule added at repo root (new file mode 160000) is almost certainly accidental and will break non-recursive checkouts/CI
invalidate_upsampling_cache() is dead code — nothing calls it on allowlist changes, so cache consistency relies solely on the 60s TTL

sum(sample_weight) assumes weights exist and are backfilled for all historical events in allowlisted projects; if pre-rollout events have NULL/0 weights, historical counts will be silently wrong — needs schema/backfill verification

Stray git submodule `sentry-repo` (gitlink, mode 160000) committed without a corresponding `.gitmodules` entry, so the URL can't be resolved and submodule checkout fails for cloners/CI; should be removed before merge

`count()` semantics silently change on the public /events-stats endpoint: when all queried projects are on the allowlist, counts are multiplied by 1/sample_rate with no opt-in parameter or response meta flag, so callers (dashboards, integrations, exports) can't distinguish upsampled from raw counts; also causes inconsistent results across cached eligibility, mixed vs single-project queries, and cross-endpoint comparisons

`upsampled_count` SnQL function is only registered for the Discover dataset, but `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns True unconditionally for the errors dataset, resulting in either dead/misleading code or query errors (400/500) for errors-dataset queries with allowlisted projects; the `sample_weight` column's existence in the errors storage schema is also assumed but not established

Error-focus heuristic uses a raw substring check (`"event.type:error" in query`) that matches negated queries (`!event.type:error`) and composite queries (`event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`), applying the upsampled transform incorrectly and yielding zero/undercounted transaction counts or snuba errors

New `upsampled_count` aggregate omits `private=True` in its SnQLFunction definition, making it part of the public query grammar so any API user can call it on any project, returning misleading zero counts for projects/events without `sample_weight`

Events without `sample_weight` are silently excluded by `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`, so for allowlisted projects any events ingested before sampling was enabled contribute 0 instead of 1, silently undercounting historical ranges; the assumed invariant is not enforced or backfilled

`invalidate_upsampling_cache` is ineffective because the cache key embeds `hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`, making invalidation on allowlist changes require enumerating every project subset; it also has no callers, so correctness relies solely on the 60s TTL while the docstring claims an invalidation-based guarantee, and the comment on `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` claiming config is read 'fresh each time' contradicts the 60s wrapper cache

upsampled_count() is only registered in the discover dataset's function_converter, but the sample weight transform is also applied to the errors dataset, so errors-dataset queries emit an unknown function and fail with a parse error (stats requests 400/500 for allowlisted orgs on that path)

Naive substring match in _is_error_focused_query ('event.type:error' in query) misclassifies negated queries (-event.type:error), mixed queries (event.type:error OR event.type:transaction), and quoted search text, applying sum(sample_weight) to data largely lacking sample_weight and yielding zero/garbage counts; it also under-matches default discover queries with no event.type filter, silently skipping upsampling where it should apply

adjudication.rationale: In `organization_events_stats._get_event_stats`, the actual query executed is the local `query` argument passed into the function, but upsampling eligibility is computed via `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(..., request)` which (for the `discover` dataset) calls `_is_error_focused_query(request)` and inspects `request.GET.get("query")` instead of the `query` string that will be executed. This is a correctness issue whenever the executed query is derived/modified separately from the raw request param (the file already imports `DashboardWidget`, implying non-GET sources/flows exist), because upsampling may be skipped or applied based on a different string than what Snuba runs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is never called anywhere in the diff and its cache key scheme (org id + hash of exact project-id tuple) cannot invalidate allowlist changes, leaving stale upsampled results for up to 60s after a project is removed from the allowlist

adjudication.rationale: In `sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`, eligibility is cached for 60s under `error_upsampling_eligible:{org_id}:{hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))}`. The diff introduces `invalidate_upsampling_cache(...)`, but nothing in the shown changes calls it. Also, because the cache key is tied to the exact queried `project_ids` tuple, an allowlist change cannot be broadly invalidated without knowing every project-id combination that might have been cached; therefore stale eligibility decisions (and thus temporarily incorrect choice to apply upsampling transforms) can persist until TTL expiry. The diff’s docstring explicitly accepts eventual consistency, so this is more of a design/consistency concern than a clear defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In the top-events branch, only `query_columns` is transformed; `equations` and `orderby` containing `count()` are left untransformed, producing inconsistent weighted vs unweighted numbers in the same response and potentially breaking orderby resolution against the `upsampled_count() as count` column

adjudication.rationale: In `organization_events_stats._get_event_stats`, the new upsampling logic only transforms the y-axis/timeseries columns (`query_columns` -> `final_columns`) via `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(...)`, but still passes `equations=self.get_equation_list(...)` and `orderby=self.get_orderby(request)` unchanged in the top-events paths (`run_top_events_timeseries_query` / `top_events_timeseries`). Since the transformation replaces `count()` with `upsampled_count() as count`, any equation or orderby expression that still uses `count()` would remain unweighted while the y-axis is weighted, yielding inconsistent results within the same response and potentially causing orderby expressions like `count()` to not match the aliased `count` output.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Naive substring check in _is_error_focused_query ("event.type:error" in query.lower()) misroutes non-error queries (negation like !event.type:error, mixed OR queries, literal text matches) into the upsampling transform, rewriting count() to sum(sample_weight) which doesn't exist for transaction events, causing user-triggerable Snuba 500s or silently wrong statistics; should parse the query via the search backend instead of substring-matching raw input

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `_is_error_focused_query()` which returns True based on a raw substring check (`if "event.type:error" in query:`) on `request.GET["query"].lower()` (src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py). That result gates `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform()` for the `discover` dataset, and ultimately rewrites `count()` into `upsampled_count() as count` (sum(sample_weight)) via `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling()` in the organization events stats endpoint. Because the check does not account for negation (`!event.type:error`), complex boolean queries, or literal text matches, it can incorrectly enable the transform for non-error result sets where `sample_weight` may not exist (the code itself states it “doesn't exist for transactions”), leading to incorrect statistics or query errors.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py`, the new `SnQLFunction("upsampled_count", ...)` is added without `private=True`, while adjacent/internal-only functions (e.g. the nearby `failure_count`) are marked `private=True`. This means `upsampled_count()` is exposed through the Discover dataset function registry and can likely be invoked directly by users in queries, bypassing the endpoint-side allowlist logic that only rewrites `count()` via `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling(...)`. Since `upsampled_count` aggregates `sum(sample_weight)` and the diff’s own helper notes `sample_weight` doesn’t exist for non-error contexts/datasets, direct usage could produce incorrect results or Snuba errors when `sample_weight` is unavailable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cache key built from Python hash() of the sorted project-ID tuple is collision-prone by design; two different project sets hashing to the same value would be served the wrong eligibility decision (upsampling applied to a non-allowlisted set or vice versa); should use a deterministic, collision-resistant encoding such as sorted IDs joined

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a cache key built as `f"error_upsampling_eligible:{organization.id}:{hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))}` in `sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py`. Using Python’s `hash()` here is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization) and can theoretically collide, which makes the cache less reliable/efficient and, in the collision case, could return an eligibility decision for the wrong project set. A deterministic encoding of the sorted IDs (e.g., `"-".join(map(str, sorted_ids))`) would avoid these issues.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds (a) query-time upsampling by transforming `count()` into `upsampled_count()` which is defined as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` in the Discover dataset, and (b) a *test factory* helper `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` that copies `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate` into `normalized_data['sample_rate']` before storing events in tests.
